definition: to agree to something, especially after thinking about it

examples.text: After a week of debate, the council assented to the treaty.
The father finally assents to the marriage he once forbade.
My parents assented to a later curfew on the condition that I text when I arrive.

confused.note: To assent is to agree; an ascent is a climb.

questions.passage: The proposal required the approval of all five board members. Four agreed at once; the fifth, after asking for another week to study the figures, at last ______ as well.
questions.explanation: The fifth member finally agreed.

distractors.why: Discriminated means distinguished between things, which does not fit.
Depreciated means fell in value, which does not fit.
Procrastinated means delayed; she asked for time, but the sentence reports that she finally agreed.

definition: stretched or pulled tight; tense

examples.text: The spider keeps each thread of its web taut.
Her face was taut with worry as the ship came into view.
Pull the tent ropes taut or the wind will take it.

confused.note: Taut means pulled tight; taught is the past tense of teach.

questions.passage: A tightrope must be kept perfectly ______. If the wire sags even a few centimeters, it will sway under the walker's weight and make balance nearly impossible.
questions.explanation: A wire that must not sag has to be pulled tight.

distractors.why: Pliable means easily bent, the opposite of a tight wire.
Cordial means warm and friendly, which does not describe a wire.
Infamous means famous for something bad, which does not fit.

definition: the quality of being fierce, violent, and intense

examples.text: The ferocity of the storm tore roofs from houses a mile inland.
The ferocity of the defenders surprised an army three times their size.
My little sister defends her fries with surprising ferocity.

confused.note: Ferocity is fierceness; veracity is truthfulness.

questions.passage: Forecasters had predicted strong winds, but no one expected the ______ of the storm that struck that night. It uprooted century-old oaks, flattened barns, and left the coast road buried under sand.
questions.explanation: A storm that uproots oaks and flattens barns is fierce and violent.

distractors.why: Fidelity is faithfulness, which does not describe a storm.
Decorum is proper behavior, which does not fit.
Consolation is comfort, which does not fit.

definition: to destroy something completely

examples.text: The plague annihilated entire villages along the trade route.
When matter meets antimatter, the two annihilate each other.
Our team was annihilated, twelve to nothing.

confused.note: To annihilate is to destroy utterly; to humiliate is to shame.

questions.passage: The eruption did not merely damage the town. It ______ it: within hours every building lay under four meters of ash, and nothing of the settlement was seen again for seventeen centuries.
questions.explanation: A town buried and lost for centuries was completely destroyed.

distractors.why: Depreciated means lost value, which is far too weak and does not fit.
Fostered means encouraged the growth of, the opposite of destroying.
Foiled means prevented a plan from succeeding, which does not fit a town.

partsNote: from Latin nihil, "nothing": to bring to nothing

definition: to treat someone cruelly or unfairly, especially because of their beliefs or identity

examples.text: The regime persecuted writers who questioned its authority.
The novel follows a family persecuted for their faith.
My brother claims he is persecuted because he has to share the remote.

confused.note: To persecute is to treat cruelly; to prosecute is to bring a legal case against.

questions.passage: For three centuries the sect was ______. Its members were barred from owning land, forbidden to hold public office, and at times driven from their homes by mobs.
questions.explanation: Being barred, forbidden, and driven out is cruel and unfair treatment.

distractors.why: Prosecuted means charged in court; the examples describe sustained cruelty, not legal trials.
Exalted means raised to high honor, the opposite of this treatment.
Delegated means assigned to another, which does not fit.

definition: not giving way to pressure or persuasion; firm

examples.text: The unyielding commander refused three offers of surrender.
The drill bit broke against the unyielding granite.
My grandmother is unyielding on one point: no phones at the table.

confused.note: Unyielding means refusing to give way; unwieldy means awkward to handle.

questions.passage: Negotiators hoped the mayor might compromise on the height of the new tower. She proved ______, repeating at every meeting that no building in the old town would ever rise above the cathedral.
questions.explanation: Repeating the same refusal at every meeting shows she would not give way.

distractors.why: Pliable means easily influenced, the opposite of her stance.
Cordial means warm and friendly, which is not the point.
Unassuming means modest, which does not describe firm refusal.

definition: to lose value over time; or to make something seem less valuable

examples.text: The currency depreciated so fast that prices were changed twice a day.
Laboratory equipment depreciates quickly as newer models appear.
A new car depreciates the moment it leaves the lot.

confused.note: To depreciate is to lose value; to deprecate is to express disapproval of.

questions.passage: Unlike a house, which often gains value, a computer begins to ______ as soon as it is purchased. A machine bought for two thousand dollars may be worth less than half that a year later.
questions.explanation: Being worth less than half a year later is losing value.

distractors.why: Appropriate as a verb means to take for one's own use, which does not fit.
Digress means to wander from the subject, which does not fit.
Attain means to achieve, which does not fit.

partsNote: from Latin pretium, "price": to lower the price

definition: to take something for your own use, usually without permission; or to set money aside for a purpose

examples.text: The crown appropriated the monasteries' lands and sold them to its supporters.
The poet was accused of appropriating whole stanzas from a forgotten rival.
My sister appropriated my charger and now denies it was ever mine.

confused.note: To appropriate is to take for one's own use; apropos means fitting or relevant.

questions.passage: The general did not ask the villagers for their horses. He simply ______ them, sending soldiers to lead the animals away and leaving behind a note promising payment after the war.
questions.explanation: Taking the horses without asking is taking them for his own use.

distractors.why: Delegated means assigned a task to someone, which does not fit horses.
Attributed means credited to a cause, which does not fit.
Divulged means revealed a secret, which does not fit.

partsNote: from Latin proprius, "one's own": to make one's own

definition: based on facts and not influenced by personal feelings or opinions

examples.text: A blind trial gives a more objective measure of whether the drug works.
No objective account of the battle survives; each side wrote its own.
I am not objective about my own cooking, so ask someone else.

confused.note: Objective means unbiased; an objection is a statement of disagreement.

questions.passage: Judges in the competition are given only a number for each entry, never the baker's name. The rule is meant to keep their decisions ______ by ensuring that friendship or reputation cannot influence the scores.
questions.explanation: Decisions free of personal influence are based on the entries alone.

distractors.why: Subjective means shaped by personal feeling, which the rule is meant to prevent.
Elaborate means detailed and complicated, which does not fit.
Insular means narrow in outlook, which does not fit.

definition: to encourage something to develop

examples.text: Warm, shallow water fosters the growth of algae.
The peace fostered trade between the two kingdoms.
Our coach fosters teamwork by rotating the captain every week.

confused.note: To foster is to encourage growth; to fester is to become infected or worse.

questions.passage: The school's founder wanted to ______ curiosity, not obedience. Students were encouraged to interrupt lessons with questions, and the best question of each week was written on a board in the entrance hall.
questions.explanation: Rewarding questions encourages curiosity to develop.

distractors.why: Foil means to prevent from succeeding, the opposite of encouraging.
Depreciate means to lose value, which does not fit.
Persecute means to treat cruelly, which does not fit.

definition: to put a plan, decision, or system into action

examples.text: The reforms were approved in 1861 but not implemented for a decade.
The hospital implemented a new protocol for washing hands.
I finally implemented my plan to pack lunch the night before.

confused.note: To implement is to carry out; to implicate is to show someone's involvement.

questions.passage: Passing the law proved easier than ______ it. Three years after the vote, the government had hired only a tenth of the inspectors needed to enforce the new rules.
questions.explanation: Putting the law into action required inspectors who were never hired.

distractors.why: Divulging means revealing a secret, which does not fit.
Exalting means praising highly, which does not fit.
Attributing means crediting to a cause, which does not fit.

definition: something that happens or exists, especially something unusual or interesting

examples.text: The northern lights are a phenomenon caused by particles from the sun.
Mass migration to the cities was a new phenomenon in the 1800s.
The phenomenon of losing one sock per wash remains unexplained.

confused.note: Phenomenon is singular; phenomena is the plural.

questions.passage: Scientists have long been puzzled by a ______ observed in certain lakes. On calm winter nights, large round holes appear in the ice, though no current, spring, or animal has been found that could explain them.
questions.explanation: An observed happening that needs explaining is a phenomenon.

distractors.why: A tenet is a principle or belief, not an observed event.
A mandate is an official order, which does not fit.
Hyperbole is exaggeration, which does not fit.

definition: containing a lot of careful detail or many parts

examples.text: The coronation followed an elaborate ritual that lasted nine hours.
The bird builds an elaborate nest of woven grass with a false entrance.
My cousin tells elaborate stories about why his homework is late.

confused.note: Elaborate means detailed; to collaborate is to work together.

questions.passage: The thieves' plan was remarkably ______. It involved forged uniforms, a tunnel dug over six months, a decoy truck, and a schedule timed to the second.
questions.explanation: A plan with many carefully prepared parts is detailed and complicated.

distractors.why: Unassuming means modest, which does not describe a complicated plan.
Taut means pulled tight, which does not fit.
Legitimate means lawful, which a theft plan is not, and it is not what the details show.

definition: an official order to do something; or the authority given by voters to a government

examples.text: The governor claimed a mandate from the people to rebuild the harbor.
The new mandate requires every lab to publish its raw data.
The school's mandate on closed-toe shoes ended sandal season.

confused.note: A mandate is an official order; mandatory means required.

questions.passage: The mayor won the election by the largest margin in the city's history. She interpreted the result as a ______ to carry out the changes she had promised, beginning with the closing of the old power plant.
questions.explanation: A large victory gives her the authority to act on her promises.

distractors.why: Consolation is comfort after a loss, which does not fit a victory.
Dissonance is a lack of harmony, which does not fit.
A pariah is an outcast, which does not fit.

partsNote: from Latin manus, "hand," and dare, "to give": given into the hand

definition: a formal agreement; a state of agreement or harmony

examples.text: The two governments signed a peace accord in the spring.
For once the sisters are in complete accord: the piano must be sold.
My parents and I reached an accord on screen time.

confused.note: An accord is an agreement; an accordion is a musical instrument.

questions.passage: After eleven months of talks, the two countries finally reached an ______. Its terms set a shared border, opened three crossing points to trade, and provided for the return of prisoners held by both sides.
questions.explanation: Terms settling border, trade, and prisoners make up a formal agreement.

distractors.why: A phenomenon is an observed event, which does not fit.
Dissonance is disagreement or clash, the opposite of reaching terms.
Hypocrisy is saying one thing and doing another, which does not fit.

definition: to say that something is caused by or belongs to a particular person or thing

examples.text: Doctors attribute the drop in infections to better hand washing.
The painting was long attributed to a student of the master.
I attribute my good mood to the extra hour of sleep.

confused.note: To attribute is to credit a cause; to contribute is to give toward something.

questions.passage: Economists ______ the town's recovery to the opening of the new railway. Before the line arrived, they note, farmers had no way of getting their crops to market before they spoiled.
questions.explanation: They credit the railway as the cause of the recovery.

distractors.why: Appropriate as a verb means to take for one's own use, which does not fit.
Delegate means to hand a task to someone, which does not fit.
Defer means to postpone or yield, which does not fit.

partsNote: from Latin tribuere, "to give": to give to

definition: to prevent someone from doing something they planned

examples.text: A sudden storm foiled the invasion fleet.
The detective foils the robbery with a single telephone call.
My plan to sleep in was foiled by the neighbor's leaf blower.

confused.note: To foil is to thwart; foul means offensive or against the rules.

questions.passage: The burglars had disabled the alarm and cut the telephone line. Their plan was ______, however, by a neighbor's dog, whose barking woke half the street before they reached the door.
questions.explanation: The dog's barking stopped the plan from succeeding.

distractors.why: Fostered means encouraged, the opposite of stopping a plan.
Implemented means carried out, but the plan failed.
Attained means achieved, which does not fit.

definition: well known for being bad or evil

examples.text: The infamous prison held political prisoners for two centuries.
The novel's infamous first sentence has been mocked for a hundred years.
Our school is infamous for its mystery meat on Thursdays.

confused.note: Famous means well known; infamous means well known for something bad.

questions.passage: The stretch of coast is ______ among sailors. Its hidden reefs have sunk more than two hundred ships, and old charts mark it simply as "the graveyard."
questions.explanation: A coast known for sinking ships is famous for something bad.

distractors.why: Cordial means warm and friendly, which does not fit.
Destitute means extremely poor, which does not describe a coast.
Exuberant means full of energy and joy, which does not fit.

partsNote: from Latin fama, "reputation": of ill fame

definition: to give part of your work, power, or authority to someone else

examples.text: The king delegated the governing of the provinces to his brothers.
The lead researcher delegated the data analysis to two students.
I delegated the dishwashing to my brother in exchange for my dessert.

confused.note: To delegate is to hand over a task; to relegate is to push to a lower position.

questions.passage: The founder insisted on approving every purchase herself, down to the pencils. As the company grew, she was forced to ______ such decisions to managers, though she never stopped checking their work.
questions.explanation: Handing decisions to managers is giving part of her authority to others.

distractors.why: Divulge means to reveal a secret, which does not fit.
Procrastinate means to delay, which does not fit handing decisions "to managers."
Depreciate means to lose value, which does not fit.

partsNote: from Latin legare, "to send as a deputy"

definition: behavior that does not match the beliefs or standards a person claims to have

examples.text: Critics attacked the hypocrisy of a government that preached thrift and built palaces.
The novel exposes the hypocrisy of a town that prays on Sunday and cheats on Monday.
It is hypocrisy to lecture me about screen time while scrolling on your phone.

confused.note: Hypocrisy is saying one thing and doing another; a hypothesis is a proposed explanation.

questions.passage: The senator who had campaigned for years against waste was found to have billed taxpayers for a private jet. Newspapers were quick to point out the ______.
questions.explanation: Condemning waste while wasting public money is failing to practice what one preaches.

distractors.why: Fidelity is faithfulness to one's commitments, the opposite of this conduct.
Decorum is proper behavior, which is not what newspapers pointed out.
Consolation is comfort, which does not fit.

definition: to succeed in getting or reaching something, usually after effort

examples.text: The colony attained independence after eight years of war.
The rocket attained a speed of eight kilometers per second.
I finally attained my goal of running five miles without stopping.

confused.note: To attain is to reach a goal through effort; to obtain is to get possession of something.

questions.passage: Few climbers ______ the summit on their first attempt. The mountain's sudden storms turn back three expeditions in four, and many who succeed have tried twice before.
questions.explanation: Reaching the summit is succeeding in getting there.

distractors.why: Defer means to postpone, which does not fit.
Foil means to prevent a plan, which does not fit climbers and a summit.
Attribute means to credit to a cause, which does not fit.

definition: comfort given to someone who is sad or disappointed

examples.text: The widow finds consolation in her garden.
The king's letter was small consolation to the families of the drowned sailors.
A free dessert was some consolation for the hour-long wait.

confused.note: Consolation is comfort; a consultation is a meeting to get advice.

questions.passage: The team lost the final by a single point. It was some ______ to the players that their captain was named the tournament's best, though most said they would gladly have traded the honor for the trophy.
questions.explanation: An honor that softens a disappointing loss is a comfort.

distractors.why: Hypocrisy is false virtue, which does not fit.
Ferocity is fierceness, which does not fit.
A mandate is an official order, which does not fit.

definition: loyalty and faithfulness; or accuracy in copying or reproducing something

examples.text: The knights swore fidelity to the young queen.
The recording reproduces the concert with remarkable fidelity.
My dog's fidelity is absolute, especially when I am holding a sandwich.

confused.note: Fidelity is loyalty or accuracy; to fidget is to move restlessly.

questions.passage: The translator was praised for her ______ to the original. She preserved not only the poem's meaning but also its rhythm, its rhymes, and even the awkward pause in its final line.
questions.explanation: Preserving meaning, rhythm, and rhyme is faithfulness to the original.

distractors.why: Hyperbole is exaggeration, the opposite of faithful accuracy.
Dissonance is a clash, which does not fit.
Decorum is proper behavior, which does not fit.

definition: to recognize a difference between things; or to treat people unfairly because of who they are

examples.text: Bees can discriminate between flowers that look identical to us.
The law discriminated against anyone who did not own land.
I cannot discriminate between the two colas, whatever my brother claims.

confused.note: To discriminate is to tell apart or treat unfairly; to incriminate is to make someone appear guilty.

questions.passage: An experienced tea taster can ______ among dozens of varieties. From a single sip she can name the region where the leaves were grown and often the month in which they were picked.
questions.explanation: Telling many varieties apart is recognizing differences.

distractors.why: Digress means to wander off the subject, which does not fit.
Assent means to agree, which does not fit.
Procrastinate means to delay, which does not fit.

definition: continuing without stopping or becoming less intense

examples.text: The relentless pounding of the waves undercut the cliff.
The army's relentless advance left the defenders no time to regroup.
My sister was relentless in asking for a puppy, and it worked.

confused.note: Relentless means never letting up; reckless means careless of danger.

questions.passage: The reporter's questioning was ______. For two hours she returned again and again to the same missing payment, rephrasing the question each time the minister tried to change the subject.
questions.explanation: Returning to the same question for two hours never lets up.

distractors.why: Cordial means warm and friendly, which is not what the details stress.
Antiquated means old-fashioned, which does not fit.
Insular means narrow in outlook, which does not fit.

definition: to delay something until a later time; or to yield to someone else's opinion or wishes

examples.text: The council deferred its decision until the envoy returned.
The team deferred the launch because of high winds.
I defer to my sister on all matters involving directions.

confused.note: To defer is to postpone or yield; to differ is to be unlike or to disagree.

questions.passage: The committee was not ready to vote. It chose to ______ the question until its next meeting, by which time members hoped to have the engineers' report in hand.
questions.explanation: Putting the question off until the next meeting is postponing it.

distractors.why: Divulge means to reveal, which does not fit.
Exalt means to praise highly, which does not fit.
Digress means to stray from the subject, and it cannot take "the question" as an object.

partsNote: to carry away, to put off

definition: firm and unchanging in loyalty or belief

examples.text: She remained a steadfast ally of the queen through three rebellions.
The dog's steadfast devotion outlasts every human friendship in the novel.
My grandfather is steadfast in his belief that his team will win this year.

confused.note: Steadfast means firm in loyalty; "in someone's stead" means in their place.

questions.passage: Many of the candidate's early supporters drifted away as the polls turned against her. A few remained ______, knocking on doors in the rain until the final hour of the campaign.
questions.explanation: Continuing to work when others left shows unchanging loyalty.

distractors.why: Pliable means easily swayed, the opposite of loyal persistence.
Insular means narrow in outlook, which does not fit.
Destitute means extremely poor, which is not the contrast with those who drifted away.

definition: warm, friendly, and polite

examples.text: Relations between the two courts were cordial but never close.
The innkeeper gives the travelers a cordial welcome and the best room.
My neighbor and I exchange cordial waves and have never learned each other's names.

confused.note: Cordial means warm and polite; a cordon is a line of guards or a barrier.

questions.passage: Observers had expected a tense meeting between the two rival chefs. To their surprise the conversation was entirely ______: the two shook hands, praised each other's restaurants, and exchanged recipes before parting.
questions.explanation: Handshakes, praise, and shared recipes show warm, friendly manners.

distractors.why: Intractable means hard to manage, which does not describe a friendly talk.
Antiquated means old-fashioned, which does not fit.
Exuberant means overflowing with excitement, stronger than a polite, friendly exchange.

definition: made up of many different kinds of people or things

examples.text: Soil is a heterogeneous mixture of minerals, water, air, and living matter.
The empire ruled a heterogeneous population speaking forty languages.
My playlist is heterogeneous: polka, rap, and whale songs.

confused.note: Heterogeneous means of many kinds; homogeneous means all of one kind.

questions.passage: The class was unusually ______. Its thirty students ranged in age from seventeen to sixty-four, came from eleven countries, and included a retired pilot, two nurses, and a former circus acrobat.
questions.explanation: Students of many ages, countries, and backgrounds make a varied group.

distractors.why: Homogeneous means all alike, the opposite of this class.
Unassuming means modest, which is not what the details show.
Subsequent means coming after, which does not fit.

partsNote: from Greek heteros, "other": of other kinds

definition: old-fashioned and no longer useful or suitable

examples.text: The fort's antiquated cannon could not reach the modern warships.
The lab replaced its antiquated microscopes with digital ones.
The school's antiquated computers take ten minutes to start.

confused.note: Antiquated means out of date and no longer useful; an antique is an old object valued for its age.

questions.passage: The hospital's record system was hopelessly ______. Patient files were still kept on paper cards in wooden drawers, and finding a single chart could take a clerk half an hour.
questions.explanation: Paper cards in drawers are out of date and inefficient.

distractors.why: Radical means extreme or fundamentally new, the opposite of an old system.
Cordial means friendly, which does not fit.
Legitimate means lawful or valid, which is not the complaint.

definition: a lack of agreement or harmony; a clash of sounds

examples.text: The dissonance between the model's predictions and the data forced a rethink.
There is a dissonance between the narrator's cheerful words and what he describes.
The dissonance of two radios playing different songs gave me a headache.

confused.note: Dissonance is a clash or lack of harmony; dissidence is open disagreement with authority.

questions.passage: Visitors often remark on the ______ between the museum's exterior and what it contains. The building is a severe concrete box, yet its galleries hold some of the most delicate lace and porcelain ever made.
questions.explanation: A severe building holding delicate objects is a clash between two things.

distractors.why: Decorum is proper behavior, which does not fit.
A tenet is a principle, which does not fit.
Hyperbole is exaggeration, which does not fit.

partsNote: from Latin sonare, "to sound": sounding apart

definition: one of the principles or beliefs that a theory or group is based on

examples.text: Free trade was a central tenet of the party's program.
A basic tenet of the method is that results must be repeatable.
A tenet of our family road trips is that the driver picks the music.

confused.note: A tenet is a principle; a tenant is a person who rents.

questions.passage: A central ______ of the school's philosophy is that children learn best by doing. Its pupils therefore spend little time at desks and a great deal in workshops, kitchens, and gardens.
questions.explanation: A belief on which a philosophy rests is a principle.

distractors.why: A pariah is an outcast, which does not fit.
A despot is a tyrant, which does not fit.
A phenomenon is an observed event, not a guiding belief.

definition: full of energy, excitement, and happiness

examples.text: The exuberant puppy knocks over the tea table in the first chapter.
Exuberant crowds filled the streets when the war ended.
My exuberant little cousin greeted me with a running hug.

confused.note: Exuberant means joyfully energetic; exorbitant means unreasonably high in price.

questions.passage: The orchestra's new conductor is as ______ as her predecessor was reserved. She leaps on the podium, sings along with the cellos, and has been known to dance offstage at the end of a concert.
questions.explanation: Leaping, singing, and dancing show energy and joy.

distractors.why: Unassuming means modest and quiet, closer to her predecessor.
Destitute means extremely poor, which does not fit.
Steadfast means loyal and unchanging, which is not what the details show.

definition: to give someone information that is supposed to be secret

examples.text: The captured spy refused to divulge the names of his contacts.
The housekeeper will not divulge what she saw that night.
I will not divulge what I got my brother for his birthday.

confused.note: To divulge is to reveal a secret; to indulge is to allow oneself a pleasure.

questions.passage: The chef has guarded the recipe for forty years. She has refused to ______ it even to her own children, saying only that it contains eleven ingredients and that one of them is patience.
questions.explanation: Refusing to reveal a guarded secret is refusing to divulge it.

distractors.why: Defer means to postpone or yield, which does not fit a recipe.
Exalt means to praise highly, which does not fit.
Procrastinate means to delay, and it cannot take "it" as an object.

definition: a way of speaking or writing that makes something sound much bigger or better than it is

examples.text: "I have told you a million times" is hyperbole.
The poster's claim of "the greatest show on Earth" was cheerful hyperbole.
Calling the cafeteria pizza "life-changing" was hyperbole.

confused.note: Hyperbole is exaggeration; a hyperbola is a curve in geometry.

questions.passage: The advertisement described the new phone as "a device that will change the course of human history." Few readers took this ______ seriously; the phone's chief improvement was a slightly larger screen.
questions.explanation: Claiming a phone will change history is wild exaggeration.

distractors.why: A tenet is a principle, not an exaggerated claim.
Decorum is proper behavior, which does not fit.
Dissonance is a clash, which does not fit "took this seriously."

partsNote: from Greek ballein, "to throw": throwing beyond

definition: very difficult to control, manage, or solve

examples.text: The disease remains intractable despite decades of research.
The border dispute proved intractable and outlasted four governments.
The tangle of cords behind the television is intractable.

confused.note: Intractable means hard to manage; intangible means unable to be touched.

questions.passage: Traffic in the old city is an ______ problem. Its streets are too narrow to widen, its buildings too precious to demolish, and every scheme proposed in the last fifty years has made matters worse.
questions.explanation: A problem that defeats every solution is very hard to solve.

distractors.why: Pliable means easily shaped or managed, the opposite of this problem.
Subsequent means coming after, which does not fit.
Cordial means friendly, which does not fit.

partsNote: not able to be pulled or led

definition: behavior that is polite and proper for a particular occasion

examples.text: The envoy's breach of decorum, sitting before the king sat, nearly ended the talks.
The aunt values decorum above happiness and says so often.
The principal reminded us to observe decorum during the graduation ceremony.

confused.note: Decorum is proper behavior; decor is the decoration of a room.

questions.passage: Members of the chamber are expected to maintain ______ at all times. They may not shout, must address one another by title, and are required to stand when the presiding officer enters.
questions.explanation: Rules about shouting, titles, and standing are standards of proper behavior.

distractors.why: Hyperbole is exaggeration, which does not fit.
Dissonance is discord, the opposite of orderly conduct.
A tenet is a principle or belief; the sentence is about conduct.

definition: not wanting to be noticed or to claim importance; modest

examples.text: The unassuming clerk turned out to be the author of the famous pamphlets.
The hero is an unassuming schoolteacher who dislikes being thanked.
The best pizza in town comes from an unassuming shop with no sign.

confused.note: Unassuming means modest; presuming or presumptuous means overstepping.

questions.passage: Visitors to the laboratory rarely guess that the ______ man refilling the coffee pot is its director. He wears no badge, never mentions his prizes, and introduces himself only by his first name.
questions.explanation: Wearing no badge and never mentioning prizes shows modesty.

distractors.why: Exuberant means lively and excited, which is not described.
Imperious means arrogant and commanding, the opposite of his modest manner.
Radical means extreme, which does not fit.

definition: to move away from the main subject when speaking or writing

examples.text: The narrator digresses for a whole chapter on the history of buttons.
The speaker digressed so often that the audience forgot his topic.
My grandfather starts a story about the war and digresses into one about a goat.

confused.note: To digress is to wander from the subject; to regress is to return to a worse state.

questions.passage: The lecture was supposed to concern volcanoes. The professor, however, tended to ______, and by the end of the hour the class had heard about his childhood dog, the price of coffee, and a train he once missed in Lisbon.
questions.explanation: Wandering to unrelated topics is straying from the subject.

distractors.why: Assent means to agree, which does not fit.
Defer means to postpone or yield, which does not capture wandering off topic.
Exalt means to praise highly, which does not fit.

definition: to delay doing something that you should do

examples.text: The hero procrastinates for three acts before taking his revenge.
The king procrastinated until the invaders were at the gates.
I procrastinated on my essay by cleaning my entire room.

confused.note: To procrastinate is to put off; to prognosticate is to predict.

questions.passage: The author admits that she tends to ______. Before writing a single page of her last novel, she repainted her study, alphabetized four hundred books, and learned to bake bread.
questions.explanation: Doing everything except writing is putting off what she should do.

distractors.why: Discriminate means to tell apart, which does not fit.
Exalt means to praise highly, which does not fit.
Attain means to achieve, which does not fit.

partsNote: from Latin cras, "tomorrow": forward to tomorrow

definition: easy to bend without breaking; or easily influenced

examples.text: Heat makes the plastic pliable enough to mold by hand.
The pliable young king signed whatever his uncle placed before him.
Leather boots become pliable after a few weeks of wear.

confused.note: Pliable means bendable or easily influenced; reliable means dependable.

questions.passage: Willow branches are ideal for weaving baskets. When soaked overnight they become so ______ that they can be bent double and tied in knots without snapping.
questions.explanation: Branches that bend double without breaking are easy to bend.

distractors.why: Taut means pulled tight, which does not describe bendable branches.
Intractable means hard to manage, the opposite of branches that bend easily.
Heterogeneous means of many kinds, which does not fit.

definition: to praise someone or something very highly; to raise in rank

examples.text: Court poets exalted the emperor as a living god.
The hymn exalts the courage of ordinary sailors.
My dad exalts his own chili as the finest in the county.

confused.note: To exalt is to praise or raise up; to exult is to rejoice.

questions.passage: The official biography does not simply praise its subject. It ______ him, describing an ordinary provincial governor as "the wisest ruler of his age" and comparing his speeches to those of the ancient orators.
questions.explanation: Calling an ordinary governor the wisest ruler raises him far above his due.

distractors.why: Persecutes means treats cruelly, the opposite of lavish praise.
Depreciates means lowers in value, the opposite of glorifying.
Delegates means assigns to another, which does not fit.

partsNote: from Latin altus, "high": to lift up

definition: without money, food, or the other things needed for life

examples.text: The fire left three hundred families destitute.
The orphan arrives in the city destitute, with one shoe and no name.
The charity collects coats for destitute families each winter.

confused.note: Destitute means extremely poor; desolate means empty or miserable.

questions.passage: The collapse of the bank left thousands of its customers ______. People who had saved for forty years found that their accounts were empty, and many had to sell their homes to buy food.
questions.explanation: Losing all savings and selling homes for food is being left without the means to live.

distractors.why: Infamous means famous for something bad, which does not fit.
Exuberant means joyful, which these customers were not.
Steadfast means loyal, which does not describe their loss.

definition: interested only in your own group or country and not open to new ideas

examples.text: The insular kingdom forbade foreign ships from entering its harbors.
The heroine escapes the insular village where every stranger is suspect.
Our club had grown insular, so we invited three other schools to join the tournament.

confused.note: Insular means narrow-minded or like an island; to insulate is to protect from heat, cold, or sound.

questions.passage: Critics describe the department as ______. Its members rarely attend conferences, cite only one another's work, and have not hired anyone trained outside the university in thirty years.
questions.explanation: Citing only themselves and never hiring outsiders shows a closed outlook.

distractors.why: Heterogeneous means varied, the opposite of a department that admits no outsiders.
Radical means extreme or fundamentally new, which does not fit.
Diverse means varied, which this department is not.

definition: a person who is rejected by society or by a group

examples.text: After the scandal, the minister was a pariah in the capital.
The village treats the miller's daughter as a pariah for refusing to marry.
I became a pariah at lunch after I spoiled the ending of the show.

confused.note: A pariah is an outcast; a piranha is a fish with sharp teeth.

questions.passage: After he testified against his colleagues, the engineer became a ______ in the industry. No firm would hire him, former friends crossed the street to avoid him, and his name was removed from the society's membership list.
questions.explanation: Being shunned and excluded by a whole industry makes him an outcast.

distractors.why: A despot is a tyrant, which does not describe someone who is shunned.
A tenet is a principle, not a person.
A benefactor is someone who gives help and is honored for it, the opposite of an outcast.

definition: a ruler with total power who uses it in a cruel and unfair way

examples.text: The despot closed every newspaper that dared to print his name without praise.
In the fable, a despot orders the tides to stop.
My older sister rules the remote like a despot.

confused.note: A despot is a tyrant; a depot is a storehouse or station.

questions.passage: History remembers the king as a ______. He dissolved the assembly, imprisoned judges who ruled against him, and declared that his own word was the only law the country needed.
questions.explanation: Dissolving the assembly and jailing judges is ruling with cruel, total power.

distractors.why: A pariah is an outcast, but the king held all the power.
A benefactor does good for others, the opposite of this ruler.
A novice is a beginner, which is not the point.

definition: happening or coming after something else

examples.text: Subsequent tests confirmed the first result.
The treaty and the subsequent peace lasted forty years.
The first pancake stuck to the pan; subsequent ones were perfect.

confused.note: Subsequent means coming after in time; consequent means happening as a result.

questions.passage: The first edition of the dictionary contained several thousand errors. Most were corrected in ______ editions, the fifth of which is still regarded as the standard.
questions.explanation: Editions that came after the first are later ones.

distractors.why: Antiquated means out of date, which does not describe corrected editions.
Radical means extreme, which does not fit.
Heterogeneous means of mixed kinds, which does not fit.

definition: relating to the most basic parts of something; or favoring extreme change

examples.text: The discovery forced a radical revision of the theory.
Radical members of the assembly demanded an end to the monarchy.
Cutting my hair short was a radical change after ten years of braids.

confused.note: Radical means fundamental or extreme; radial means arranged like rays from a center.

questions.passage: The new director did not propose small adjustments. Her plan was ______: she would close half the company's factories, sell its oldest brand, and move the headquarters to another continent.
questions.explanation: Closing factories and moving continents is extreme, fundamental change.

distractors.why: Cordial means friendly, which does not fit.
Unassuming means modest, the opposite of so sweeping a plan.
Subsequent means coming later, which does not fit.

partsNote: from Latin radix, "root": going to the root

definition: very different from each other; of many different kinds

examples.text: The reef supports a diverse community of more than a thousand species.
The port city was diverse, home to traders from three continents.
The food court is diverse enough that all five of us found something we liked.

confused.note: Diverse means varied; "divers" is an old word for several.

questions.passage: The panel was chosen to be as ______ as possible. Its nine members included a farmer, a surgeon, a poet, a retired general, and a student still in her first year of university.
questions.explanation: Members from many walks of life make a varied panel.

distractors.why: Insular means closed and narrow, the opposite of a varied panel.
Antiquated means out of date, which does not fit.
Taut means pulled tight, which does not fit.

definition: allowed by law; fair and reasonable

examples.text: The assembly declared her the legitimate heir to the throne.
Reviewers raised legitimate concerns about the size of the sample.
"My alarm did not go off" is a legitimate excuse exactly once.

confused.note: Legitimate means lawful or valid; legible means clear enough to read.

questions.passage: Not every complaint the company receives is frivolous. Some raise ______ concerns, such as the customer who pointed out that the product's warning label was printed in type too small to read.
questions.explanation: A concern about an unreadable warning label is fair and reasonable.

distractors.why: Infamous means famous for something bad, which does not fit.
Radical means extreme, which is not the contrast with "frivolous."
Insular means narrow in outlook, which does not fit.
